mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points within a month suggests a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer spending and business confidence improve.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances when UNRATE decreases by more than 0.3 percentage points within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over two consecutive months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the broader economy benefits from increased construction activity.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods following two consecutive months of increased HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within two months signals a weakening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as production slowdowns impact corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO decreases by more than 1% within two months.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points in the same month, it signals a robust labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200k & UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances when both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% within two months signals a strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings benefit from increased sales.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances when RSAFS increases by more than 1% within two months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals an inflationary environment with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real returns are eroded and borrowing costs increase.
regime_hint: inflationary period with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and economic activity improve.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods following two consecutive quarters of increased GDPC1.
